USA.note: World's #1 tree-nut producer/exporter (USDA FAS Tree Nuts MY2024/25). Almonds ~1,120 kt shelled (exp ~925 kt, India #1 market), walnuts, pistachios ~500 kt in-shell (off-year). ~39% of world tree-nut output (INC).

TUR.note: World's #1 hazelnut producer (~60-65% of global). 2024 crop frost-hit; hazelnut exports ~250-300 kt to the EU (Germany/Italy) for Ferrero/confectionery.

IRN.note: Pistachios in the on-year of the alternate-bearing cycle drove record world pistachio exports ~650 kt. Iran exports ~190-230 kt pistachios, China the top destination. Sanctions route via UAE/Turkey.

CHN.note: #2 tree-nut producer (walnuts/chestnuts) AND the largest single importer. China-reported HS0802 imports 2024 ~445 kt: USA 149, Australia 109, South Africa 83 (macadamias), Iran 41 (pistachios), Mexico 18.

IND.note: HS0802 tree-nut imports 2024 ~423 kt (Comtrade, India-reported): mostly US almonds (~285), Chile walnuts (37), Iran pistachios (23), Australia almonds (26). India is #1 destination for US almonds. Also a large raw-cashew processor.

VNM.note: World's #1 cashew-kernel exporter (record ~765 kt kernels in 2024, ~US$4.6bn; cashews are HS0801). Imports ~2.6 Mt raw cashew (West Africa/Cambodia) for its shellers. A processing hub, not a grower.

CIV.note: World's largest raw-cashew (HS0801) producer ~1.0-1.1 Mt in 2024. Exports raw nuts to Vietnam/India for shelling; domestic processing scaling to ~350 kt.

DEU.note: One of the largest tree-nut importers and the EU's nut-trading/re-export hub. Sources US almonds/walnuts, Turkish/Italian hazelnuts, Iranian pistachios, Vietnamese cashews, re-exports across the EU.

NLD.note: Europe's primary nut entrepot (Rotterdam): imports US almonds/walnuts, Vietnamese cashews, Turkish hazelnuts, re-exports ~80-90% onward to Germany, Poland, France, UK.

ESP.note: EU's largest almond grower (~340-400 kt in-shell) and a processor/re-exporter. Imports US almonds to top up its shelling/marzipan industry.

ITA.note: Major hazelnut grower (#2 to Turkey) and home to Ferrero's core demand. Imports Turkish hazelnuts and US almonds/pistachios/walnuts for confectionery.

CHL.note: Fast-growing Southern-Hemisphere walnut/almond exporter (counter-seasonal). 2024 walnut crop ~170-180 kt in-shell; CHL->IND ~37 kt walnuts (India-reported).

AUS.note: #2 almond exporter after the US and a major macadamia producer. China-reported HS0802 imports from Australia ~109 kt in 2024 (almonds), plus India and the Gulf.

ARE.note: Gulf re-export and distribution hub (Dubai/Jebel Ali). Imports US/Iranian pistachios (sanctions-era re-export channel), Turkish and Indian product, re-exports across MENA/South Asia. Did not report HS0802 to Comtrade 2024.

MEX.note: Significant pecan/walnut producer-exporter and a US-almond importer. China-reported HS0802 imports from Mexico ~18 kt in 2024.

GBR.note: Pure net importer of tree nuts (negligible domestic production), sourcing US almonds/walnuts, Turkish/EU hazelnuts and Vietnamese cashews for retail, snacking, bakery.

flows.note: UN Comtrade 2024 (India-reported, HS0802): India imported 285 kt of US tree nuts — almost entirely California almonds. India is the #1 destination for US almonds; the largest tree-nut bilateral flow.
UN Comtrade 2024 (China-reported, HS0802): China imported 149 kt of US tree nuts (almonds, pistachios, walnuts), ~US$0.81bn.
UN Comtrade 2024 (China-reported, HS0802): China imported 109 kt of Australian tree nuts, overwhelmingly almonds. Australia's counter-seasonal crop makes China its #1 market.
UN Comtrade 2024 (China-reported, HS0802): China imported 83 kt from South Africa, chiefly macadamias plus some almonds. South Africa is the top macadamia exporter.
UN Comtrade 2024 (China-reported, HS0802): China imported 41 kt of Iranian pistachios in the on-year. China is Iran's top pistachio market.
UN Comtrade 2024 (China-reported, HS0802): China imported 18 kt of Mexican tree nuts (pecans/walnuts).
UN Comtrade 2024 (India-reported, HS0802): India imported 37 kt of Chilean walnuts — counter-seasonal supply.
UN Comtrade 2024 (India-reported, HS0802): India imported 26 kt of Australian almonds — India's #2 almond supplier after the US.
UN Comtrade 2024 (India-reported, HS0802): India imported 23 kt of Iranian pistachios.
UN Comtrade 2024 (India-reported, HS0802): India imported 11 kt from Afghanistan (pine nuts, almonds, pistachios) via overland trade.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Germany imported 115 kt of US tree nuts (almonds, walnuts, pistachios). Germany is the EU's nut-trading hub, re-exporting onward.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: the Netherlands imported 110 kt of US tree nuts into Rotterdam for EU re-export.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Turkey imported 126 kt from the US — largely almonds for processing/snacking.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Canada imported 126 kt of US tree nuts. The US is Canada's overwhelming nut supplier.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Spain imported 104 kt of US almonds to supplement its own crop for shelling, marzipan and EU re-export.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Italy imported 75 kt of US tree nuts for its confectionery industry (Ferrero and others).
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Japan imported 55 kt of US tree nuts. The US is Japan's dominant supplier.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: South Korea imported 45 kt of US tree nuts (almonds, walnuts) for snacking.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: the UK imported 34 kt of US tree nuts for retail and bakery.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Germany imported 48 kt of Turkish hazelnuts — core raw material for German/EU confectionery (Ferrero, Storck).
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Italy imported 37 kt of Turkish hazelnuts, feeding Ferrero's plants and Italian confectionery.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: France imported 17 kt of Turkish hazelnuts for confectionery and bakery.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: the US imported 158 kt from Vietnam — predominantly cashew kernels (HS0801). The US is Vietnam's #1 cashew market.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: the Netherlands imported 50 kt of Vietnamese cashew kernels (HS0801), Rotterdam being the EU gateway.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Germany imported 37 kt of Vietnamese cashew kernels (HS0801) for retail/snacking.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: the UK imported 23 kt of Vietnamese cashew kernels (HS0801).
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: India imported 149 kt of raw cashew (HS0801) from Cote d'Ivoire for shelling. The largest West-Africa->India raw-cashew leg.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: India imported 216 kt of raw cashew (HS0801) from Tanzania — the largest East-Africa->India raw-cashew flow.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: India imported 168 kt of raw cashew (HS0801) from Togo (much transit origin).
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: India imported 162 kt of raw cashew (HS0801) from Ghana for shelling.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: India imported 123 kt of raw cashew (HS0801) from Guinea-Bissau, one of the most cashew-dependent economies.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: India imported 65 kt of raw cashew (HS0801) from Burkina Faso.
FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Germany imported 27 kt of Spanish almonds/nuts for re-export and confectionery.

FAOSTAT TCL 2024: Poland imported 21 kt of nuts re-exported via the Netherlands.

rankings.note: Tree-nut (HS0802) volumes in kt, 2024, blending USDA FAS Tree Nuts PSD, UN Comtrade 2024 importer-reports (China 445, India 423 confirmed) and FAOSTAT TCL. CAVEAT: the global nut basket spans HS0802 (tree nuts: almonds, walnuts, pistachios, hazelnuts, macadamias) AND HS0801 (cashews). Vietnam, Cote d'Ivoire and India's West-African raw-cashew flows are HS0801 — included because they dominate the broader edible-nut trade, flagged in each note. USA leads HS0802 exports; Germany/China/Netherlands/India lead imports.

companies.name: Olam Food Ingredients (ofi)
companies.note: World's largest cashew processor and a top almond/hazelnut supplier; ofi revenue ~US$15bn+ (FY2024). Vertically integrated across West-African/Vietnamese raw-cashew origination, shelling, and almond/hazelnut supply.
companies.improve: Should publish farm-gate price transparency and traceability for West-African cashew origination (smallholder income/child-labour risk) plus California almond water-use intensity.

companies.name: Blue Diamond Growers
companies.note: World's largest almond processor; a California grower-owned co-op of ~3,000 growers handling ~a third of the state's crop (~US$1.5bn). Exports to India, EU, China, Middle East.
companies.improve: Should disclose grower-level water-use efficiency and the share of acreage under regulated-deficit irrigation given drought-prone California.

companies.name: The Wonderful Company
companies.note: Owner of Wonderful Pistachios & Almonds — the world's largest pistachio grower/processor. Vertically integrated Central Valley orchards; exports heavily to China, EU, India.
companies.improve: Should disclose its Kern County water footprint and aquifer-drawdown exposure given pistachio acreage expansion into water-stressed districts.

companies.name: Ferrero Group
companies.note: World's largest single buyer of hazelnuts (~25-30% of global supply); ~EUR 18bn revenue. Effectively sets the world hazelnut price; diversifying from Turkey's frost-exposed single-origin concentration into Chile/Georgia/Serbia.
companies.improve: Should publish audited coverage of its hazelnut charter against seasonal child-labour risk in Turkish harvesting (migrant/Syrian-refugee labour).

companies.name: Borges Agricultural & Industrial Nuts
companies.note: Leading EU tree-nut processor/marketer (almonds, walnuts, pistachios, hazelnuts). Vertically integrated Spanish grower-processor; imports US/Chilean nuts to complement domestic supply and re-exports across Europe.
companies.improve: Should report origin split and water-stewardship standards for Iberian almond expansion straining Spanish aquifers.

companies.name: Vietnamese cashew cluster (Long Son, Tan Long via VINACAS)
companies.note: Vietnam's shelling cluster processes ~2.6 Mt of raw cashew into a record ~765 kt of kernel exports (2024) — the dominant node in global cashew processing for 18 straight years.
companies.improve: Should disclose energy use and labour conditions in manual shelling/peeling lines and traceability back to West-African farm origins.

global.note: World tree-nut/edible-nut totals, kt, blending INC Statistical Yearbook (world tree-nut production ~5.97 Mt 2024/25 kernel basis) with FAOSTAT and USDA PSD trade. By type: almonds ~26%, cashews ~21%, walnuts ~20%, pistachios ~19%, hazelnuts ~9%. By country: USA ~39%, China ~12%, Turkey ~10%. Export figure includes the large cashew (HS0801) trade alongside HS0802.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO/INC envelope; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6. Tree-nut demand grows ~3-4%/yr on health-snacking trends, supply led by US/Australian almond, Chilean/Chinese walnut, West-African cashew-processing expansion, tempered by California water constraints and Turkish hazelnut climate risk.
